This document defines Chirality AI Ltd.'s professional practice standard for AI agent systems in regulated engineering practice.
The standard establishes how the firm satisfies professional obligations when licensed professionals rely on AI agent work.
CHIRALITY_FRAMEWORK.md defines the theoretical foundation for knowledge in professional practice and AI-output accountability.
AI can accelerate engineering work but cannot inherit professional responsibility.
Professional engineering is a duty-of-care practice requiring accountable commitments under uncertainty and reviewable evidence.
AI changes drafting, searching, reconciling, and summarizing costs without changing requirements for competence, judgment, verification, responsibility, and durable records.
The standard is grounded in specified sections of the Engineering and Geoscience Professions Act.
The standard is grounded in General Regulation Parts 7 and 8 and Sections 49 and 54.
The standard relies on APEGA's Relying on the Work of Others and Outsourcing practice standard.
The standard relies on APEGA's Authenticating Professional Work Products practice standard.
The standard relies on APEGA's Professional Practice Management Plans guideline.
The standard applies when Chirality AI Ltd. licensed professionals use AI agent systems for PWPs under Alberta or APEGA jurisdiction.
AI agents producing work under a licensed professional's direction are treated as others whose work the professional relies on under APEGA Section 3.0.
The professional's obligations are defined by what the licensed professional must do, not by the worker's nature.
The same professional obligations apply whether work is produced by a junior engineer, engineering intern, contractor, or AI agent.
AI agents assume no professional responsibility, so responsibility flows to the licensed professional authenticating the PWP.
The AI-agent responsibility model is analogous to an unlicensed individual working under direct supervision and control.
APEGA's practice standard does not require an AI-specific amendment because obligations are to supervise, review, and authenticate.
The governance architecture makes existing obligations satisfiable for AI outputs that are plausible by construction and lack intrinsic grounding signals.
Direct supervision and control occurs when a licensed professional directs AI agents through governed scope, constraints, write boundaries, and review gates.
The agent instruction architecture is the documented framework for direct supervision and control over AI agent work.
A licensed professional's review of AI agent outputs before authentication constitutes thorough review.
APEGA Section 3.1.2.1 requires review of the relevancy and accuracy of tools used in PWP preparation.
AI model-based agent systems are technologies whose relevancy and accuracy must be reviewed before PWP authentication.
Licensed Professional means an individual entitled by the EGP Act to practise engineering in Alberta.
In the Chirality system, the Licensed Professional is the P.Eng. operating the agent system and authenticating PWPs.
Permit Holder means an entity holding a Permit to Practice under the EGP Act.
Chirality AI Ltd. is the Permit Holder for this standard.
Responsible Member means the APEGA licensed professional overseeing the permit holder's engineering practice.
Professional Work Product means an output of professional services containing technical information relied on for decisions or actions.
In the Chirality system, PWPs are authenticated deliverables issued for reliance.
Authentication means a licensed professional has completed, thoroughly reviewed, or directly supervised the work and accepts professional responsibility.
In the Chirality system, authentication corresponds to human approval, seal, and signature at the issuance gate.
Validation means a Responsible Member reviews a PWP to ensure it meets PPMP QC/QA measures.
Direct Supervision and Control means directing, monitoring, and controlling engineering work, including all practice-related decisions.
In the Chirality system, Direct Supervision and Control is gate-controlled agent orchestration with human authority at every gate.
Thorough Review means evaluating professional-service outputs prepared by others for reliability, validity, and technical accuracy.
In the Chirality system, Thorough Review is implemented by the REVIEW 5-gate protocol and a human authentication decision.
Due Diligence means the judgment, care, forethought, and determination reasonably used to avoid harm.
In the Chirality system, Due Diligence is exercised at every gate and supported by the evidence trail.
An AI Agent is a controlled architecture of model, instructions, tools, file access, and governance performing bounded work under professional direction.
In the Chirality system, an AI Agent is an AGENT_*.md instruction file instantiated at runtime.
Agent Instruction Architecture is the framework of instruction files, governance documents, invariant contracts, and deterministic tools for supervising AI agents.
The Agent Instruction Architecture consists of the agents, docs, and tools directories governed by release engineering.
Professional obligations bind any workflow that produces work product for regulated engineering practice.
Protection of the public, property, and environment is the overriding professional obligation.
When safety conflicts with commercial pressure, schedule, or convenience, safety prevails.
The public-welfare obligation is non-delegable to AI systems.
Professional liability is personal and non-transferable.
A licensed professional retains decision rights for scope and boundary decisions.
A licensed professional retains decision rights for governing codes, standards, and design basis.
A licensed professional retains decision rights for hazard and risk acceptance, including residual risk statements.
A licensed professional retains decision rights for conflict adjudication requiring engineering judgment.
A licensed professional retains decision rights for approval, issuance, signature, seal, and transmittal for reliance.
No AI system may claim to certify, approve, sign, seal, or issue engineering work for reliance.
AI agent outputs are drafts and structured assistance until human acceptance makes them engineering work product.
K-AUTH-1 enforces that only humans author binding approval records.
K-AUTH-1 prohibits agents from claiming to certify, approve, sign, seal, or issue work for reliance.
A licensed professional must not use an AI agent for work they cannot verify manually.
Using AI to produce work that cannot be adequately reviewed is a competence failure under the EGP Act.
An AI assertion alone is never a defensible basis of design.
APEGA Section 3.1.2.1 requires thorough review of the relevancy and accuracy of applicable tools used in PWP preparation.
For AI agent systems, the licensed professional must understand the agent's protocol, write scope, and constraints.
For AI agent systems, the licensed professional must understand that outputs are drafts requiring verification.
For AI agent systems, the licensed professional must know how to verify outputs against source materials and engineering judgment.
For AI agent systems, the licensed professional must understand LLM failure modes including hallucination, omission, and plausible error.
Engineering practice does not accept plausibility alone as evidence.
The firm's practice requires inputs and sources because provenance is mandatory.
The firm's practice requires assumptions to be explicitly labeled rather than hidden in prose.
The firm's practice requires methodology to be documented and reproducible.
The firm's practice requires verification evidence to be traceable to specific checks.
The firm's practice requires uncertainty and limitations to be stated.
K-PROV-1, K-INVENT-1, and K-CONFLICT-1 enforce provenance, no invention, and explicit conflict surfacing.
Technical matters follow an authority hierarchy of laws, codes, specifications, verified analysis, and professional judgment.
AI agent outputs carry no professional authority.
AI agent outputs are decision support unless explicitly accepted and issued by an accountable professional.
The direct-supervision section defines how the firm satisfies APEGA Section 3.1.1 for AI-produced work incorporated into PWPs.
APEGA requires licensed professionals to demonstrate active involvement through ongoing interaction and input.
Type 1 Manager agents operate through gate-controlled workflows where the licensed professional makes consequential decisions at every phase.
Type 2 Specialist agents execute only within bounded briefs defined by a licensed professional or authorized Type 1 agent.
Human authority is the halting condition for agent workflows.
No agent may autonomously advance workflow stages, approve deliverables, or resolve conflicts.
K-GATE-1 and K-SEAL-1 enforce dynamic gates and sealed context before Type 2 execution.
Every agent instruction file declares agent type, class, interaction surface, write scope, blocking behavior, outputs, and invariants.
K-WRITE-1 requires every agent to declare explicit write scope and prohibits writing outside it.
The Type 0, Type 1, and Type 2 hierarchy establishes authority boundaries with authority flowing downward and escalation upward.
A Type 2 agent cannot modify Type 0 rules, and a Type 1 agent cannot approve deliverables for external reliance.
Type 1 agents maintain interactive sessions with the licensed professional and await human decisions at gates.
Type 2 agents receive INIT-TASK briefs and return run reports with PASS/FAIL status and evidence.
Session handoff artifacts maintain continuity across sessions without hidden state.
AUDIT_AGENTS verifies agent instructions against the canonical standard.
Agent behavior is governed by R1-R9 workflow requirements, I1-I10 decomposition invariants, and 21 system-wide K-invariants.
The evaluation framework provides systematic assessment of agent output quality.
Agent instruction governance follows release engineering with versioning, review, and no silent behavior changes.
The REVIEW agent implements a formal 5-gate review process for lifecycle transitions.
The RECONCILIATION agent performs cross-deliverable coherence analysis.
All agent outputs are git-committed to enable diff-based review.
APEGA requires the licensed professional to be responsible for all technical engineering decisions.
Licensed professionals document relevant issues through structured context, dependency, and reference files.
Technical direction is provided through agent briefs, gate decisions, and conflict adjudication at human gates.
Licensed professionals review and approve decisions through interactive Type 1 sessions and gate-controlled workflows.
All decisions are recorded in versioned files.
A decision not recorded in a versioned file does not exist for reliance purposes.
APEGA Section 3.1.1 requires the PPMP to describe direct supervision and control and record keeping.
Agent instruction files document each agent's scope, duties, authorities, and constraints.
Governance documents define design philosophy, physical specifications, domain vocabulary, invariant contracts, and design basis.
Git history records all project state, including agent outputs, human decisions, and lifecycle transitions.
Immutable snapshots provide a timestamped append-only audit trail for analysis outputs.
The thorough-review section defines how the firm satisfies APEGA Section 3.1.2 before authentication.
Thorough review applies to all AI agent outputs incorporated into PWPs.
Thorough review is conducted before authentication even when direct supervision and control occurred throughout the work.
The licensed professional confirms reliability, accuracy, and validity by reviewing defined categories of work content and context.
Thorough review includes scope of the work, including work done by any agent.
Thorough review includes relevant design and operational conditions, including risk assessments and mitigation strategies.
Thorough review includes assumptions, limitations, and caveats supported by epistemic labeling.
Thorough review includes suitability for intended purpose and compliance with local conditions.
Thorough review includes health, safety, and environmental implications.
Thorough review includes integrity and validity of all work products, including cross-deliverable consistency.
Thorough review includes applicable calculations, analyses, evaluations, and interpretations.
Thorough review includes applicable materials and methods of construction, inspection, maintenance, or operation.
Thorough review includes relevancy and accuracy of AI agent tools used in preparing the work.
Thorough review includes interdisciplinary reviews where work crosses discipline boundaries.
The REVIEW agent implements a structured five-gate review process.
Gate 1 is a precondition check where the agent validates and the human confirms scope.
Gate 2 generates checklists from specifications, decomposition, and dependencies, with human confirmation of completeness.
Gate 3 captures findings iteratively from human-provided findings and agent-recorded evidence.
Gate 4 reviews dispositions, with the human ruling on all findings.
Gate 5 makes the lifecycle transition decision, with agent recommendation and human approval.
Transition readiness criteria are severity-based and follow the lifecycle state machine.
For IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING, all CRITICAL findings must have non-TBD human disposition.
For CHECKING to ISSUED, all CRITICAL findings must be resolved and MAJOR findings resolved or deferred with rationale.
Thorough review must verify compliance with the EGP Act and the General Regulation.
Thorough review must verify compliance with APEGA practice standards, bulletins, and guidelines.
Thorough review must verify contractual requirements for project-specific regulatory approvals or permits.
Agent instruction invariants enforce the hierarchy of authority and prevent agents from overriding codes, standards, or specifications.
Thorough review must verify that PWPs follow QC/QA processes defined in this standard and the PPMP.
Thorough review must verify that deliverables are clear, readable, consistent, and complete.
A licensed professional may authenticate a PWP only after direct supervision and control or thorough review.
Authentication requires the licensed professional to be competent to verify the work.
Authentication requires Responsible Member validation under the firm's PPMP.
Authentication binds to a specific git SHA.
Content change after authentication voids the authentication.
A deliverable is dirty if any governed input changed since its last approved SHA.
Merge to main is allowed only when branch HEAD equals the approved SHA.
The licensed professional's signature and seal apply to the specific work version identified by the SHA.
The firm's QC/QA for AI-assisted work is implemented through the agent instruction architecture.

Agent instruction files are controlled documents within the firm's quality system.
Agent instruction files are versioned in git and auditable.
Agent instruction files are reviewed before release.
Silent behavior changes to agent instruction files are not permitted.
Material changes to write scope, tool access, or outputs require review and a recorded release note.
AUDIT_AGENTS verifies agent instruction conformance against the canonical standard and structural requirements.
The firm enforces a clear boundary between deterministic operations and probabilistic operations.
Tasks that can be validated by schema or algorithm are implemented as deterministic tools rather than LLM reasoning.
LLM-based agents are reserved for work requiring inference under uncertainty.
The tool registry indexes all deterministic tools.
The firm uses vendor-provided LLMs as the cognitive engine within the agent system.
The LLM provider supplies a technology component and does not provide professional services or assume professional responsibility.
The firm's licensed professionals bear full responsibility for work produced using LLM technology.
The firm exercises due diligence on LLM technology under APEGA tool-review requirements.
LLM due diligence includes evaluating model capabilities and limitations for the firm's professional services.
LLM due diligence includes assessing model safety practices, alignment research, and responsible deployment policies.
LLM due diligence includes testing agent behavior within the instruction architecture before adopting model updates.
LLM due diligence includes documenting material model changes and their impact on agent behavior.
The agent instruction architecture constrains LLM behavior independently of provider controls.
The firm does not rely solely on model-provider safety measures.
All project truth lives in git-tracked plain files.
The firm uses no external database or hidden state for project truth.
Version control provides meaningful diffs for review, reproducibility, rollback, and audits.
Task-agent analysis outputs are written to timestamped folders that are never modified after creation.
The snapshot trail is the audit trail.
Every non-trivial governed claim cites its source file and section reference or carries a location-TBD marker.
Dependency rows are a schema-specific instance of the provenance rule.
All claims are labeled as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
Epistemic labels show whether a value is grounded or inferred.
The firm maintains records for AI-assisted work as required for PPMP compliance.

Design decision records capture what was decided, when, why, and alternatives considered.
Dependency registers provide structured dependency tracking with provenance.
_CONTEXT.md provides scope traceability for deliverables.
_REFERENCES.md provides source document pointers with relevance statements.
Analysis snapshots provide timestamped immutable records of every analysis run.
Agent run reports record inputs, outputs, quality checks, and warnings.
Review records include checklists, finding registers, disposition records, and transition decisions.
Change records include change assessments, impact analysis, and approval records.
Git version history provides a complete diff-based record of all project state changes.
Project records are retained according to the firm's PPMP and applicable regulatory requirements.
Git history provides indefinite retention of all versioned project state.

AI is compatible with regulated professional engineering when engineered into a controlled system with bounded actions and auditability.
AI compatibility with regulated practice requires monitoring, recovery, human decision rights, and human professional responsibility.
